pending_articles.title: Neuronal avalanches in awake macaque V1 and V4
pending_articles.content: Neuronal avalanches are cascades of synchronised activity whose sizes follow power law. Analyses of avalanches shed light on cortical dynamics operating near a critical point. In awake monkeys, avalanches were found in motor and premotor cortex, where they are invariant to temporal binning, detection threshold and the number of electrodes employed. Whether awake primate early visual cortex, which receives strong structured afferent drive, shares these properties has not been tested. We analyzed a public 1,024-channel resting-state dataset from V1 and V4 of two macaques. In both animals avalanche sizes followed power laws over more than 10-fold range, the exponent scaled with bin width as alpha proportional to delta-t to the power beta (beta = -0.045 and -0.031), and the distributions ended at a cutoff proportional to the number of electrodes analysed. Raising the detection threshold from 1.5 to 4.5 standard deviations (SDs) removed over 99% of events but changed alpha by only 0.02-0.05 per SD, whereas randomly removing the same events destroyed the power law. Per-electrode shuffling abolished all heavy tails. Eye closure shifted alpha, beta and the branching ratio by less than predefined equivalence bounds, far below the reproducible differences between recording sites. Avalanche organisation therefore extends to awake early visual cortex.
pending_articles.author: Solovyeva, K., Popov, P., Makarova, A., Lebedev, M.

pending_articles.title: Striatal D2-neurons gate D1-mediated associative encoding under uncertainty
pending_articles.content: Goal-directed actions are established through the encoding of predictive relationships between behaviour and its consequences, a process involving dopamine-dependent plasticity in the dorsal striatum. Early phases of learning entail complex associative landscapes from which useful action-outcome contingencies must be identified. Although dopamine processes are central to associative learning, the cellular mechanisms through which behaviourally relevant plasticity is selected from competing signalling events remain unknown. Here we show that D2-spiny projection neurons (D2-SPNs) are transiently recruited during the earliest stages of instrumental learning, when critical action-outcome contingencies emerge. We identify a dominant cell-to-cell transmodulation process by which D2-SPNs regulate dopamine-dependent signalling by constraining protein kinase A activity in D1-SPNs. This mechanism overrides extracellular dopamine signals and can be reproduced in vivo through calibrated optogenetic activation of cAMP signalling. Enhancing D2[->]D1-SPN transmodulation during uncertain reinforcement schedules durably improves action-outcome encoding, revealing a mechanism through which striatal networks promote relevant contingencies under associative ambiguity.

pending_articles.title: History of opioid use disorder correlates with altered neuroimmune signatures in the human dorsal root ganglia
pending_articles.content: Understanding mechanisms for the negative reinforcing effects of opioids are fundamental to improving patient care. Using human dorsal root ganglia (DRG) from donors with and without opioid use disorder (OUD), we set out to examine functional and molecular correlates of chronic opioid use. At a molecular level, we detected disrupted immune signatures throughout cells in the peripheral nervous system (PNS), spanning glial-neuroimmune interactions to changes in non-neuronal senescence. At the physiological level these changes are paired with sensitization of DRG sensory neurons. Our findings reveal a neuro-inflammatory state in the PNS of individuals with OUD. Targeting therapeutics towards these PNS-based mechanisms could be an approach to alleviating the negative reinforcing effects of opioids.

Central platelet-rich plasma administration promotes weight loss in diet-induced obese mice
recently_processed.content: Aims: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) contains diverse bioactive factors, but its potential role in central regulation of energy balance remains unexplored. This study investigated whether central PRP administration alters metabolic homeostasis in diet-induced obese (DIO) mice and examined associated hypothalamic responses under obese and inflammatory conditions. Materials and Methods: PRP was administered intracerebroventricularly in mouse models of DIO and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced systemic inflammation. Body weight, food intake, energy metabolism, and adiposity were assessed alongside hypothalamic microglial morphology and transcriptomic profiling. Results: A single intracerebroventricular PRP injection reduced body weight in DIO mice, with the effect persisting throughout the 7-day observation period. PRP also decreased cumulative food intake, relative gonadal white adipose tissue weight, and fasting glucose, accompanied by increased energy expenditure, oxygen consumption, fat utilization, and physical activity. In both DIO and LPS-treated mice, PRP reduced IBA1-positive area per microglial cell in the arcuate nucleus without altering microglial number. Hypothalamic RNA sequencing revealed changes in immune and metabolic signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and growth-related pathways, suggesting a complex transcriptional response rather than uniform suppression of inflammation. Conclusions: A single central PRP administration induces sustained weight loss and favorable metabolic changes in DIO mice, accompanied by region-specific hypothalamic microglial and transcriptional responses. These findings identify central PRP as a potential modulator of energy balance and provide a basis for investigating its active components and underlying mechanisms.

recently_processed.title: Starting strong: A descending analgesic dosing scheme enhances pain relief compared to a conventional ascending dosing scheme
recently_processed.content: Managing pain while minimizing opioid-related harm remains a central clinical challenge. Enhancing drug-related placebo effects has been proposed as one strategy for reducing opioid consumption, yet current dosing guidelines which recommend starting analgesic treatment at a low dose and titrating upward may inadvertently generate negative treatment expectations, since initial drug encounters are often associated with minimal pain relief. This study tested whether the inverse approach of a descending dosing scheme that starts with a strong analgesic dose more effectively enhances placebo-related analgesia than the conventional ascending scheme. Eighty-two healthy participants underwent a heat pain paradigm involving a sham analgesic treatment delivered at three different efficacy levels (low, medium, high). Participants were randomly assigned to a descending (high-to-low) or ascending (low-to-high) treatment-history sequence before receiving an identical, medium-intensity treatment during a subsequent test phase. The descending group showed significantly greater pain relief during the test phase than the ascending group, despite receiving identical treatment. These findings suggest that initiating analgesic treatment with a high, effective dose can amplify placebo-related analgesia relative to conventional dosing schemes, offering a potential strategy for reducing cumulative opioid use without compromising pain relief.
recently_processed.author: Mintah, M., Daunizeau, J., Tinnermann, A.

recently_processed.title: CortexDecoder: fMRI-to-image Reconstruction from Cortical Flatmaps
recently_processed.content: Recent advances in brain decoding work has shown the potential of Vision Transformers (ViTs) to learn mappings from neural representation to visual features. Here we present CortexDecoder, a brain decoding framework mapping fMRI flatmaps to images viewed by subjects. Flatmaps are neural responses projected onto cortical surfaces and then unfolded into 2D images. We demonstrate that (1) flatmaps preserve sufficient signal to achieve high performance in brain decoding; raw fMRI data has noisy signals and high-dimensionality which makes decoding a difficult task. (2) Reshaping raw fMRI data into flatmaps allows for clean patch-based tokenization. This allows us to harness state-of-the-art Vision Transformers to learn meaningful neural representations and preserve spatial encoding. To do this, we pass flatmap patches into a pretrained CortexMAE encoder to obtain brain tokens. A lightweight cross-attention bridge then learns to map these brain tokens to image features. Our cross-attention bridge is split into two modules; the semantic module for predicting CLIP embeddings and the lower-level module to generate low-level image reconstruction. Finally, a fine-tuned SDXL (Stable Diffusion XL) takes this low-level reconstruction image as the initial image. Conditioned by the CLIP semantic embedding, the SDXL produces the final reconstruction image. In single-subject evaluations, CortexDecoder achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art brain decoding methods, demonstrating the effectiveness of flatmap based neural representations for visual reconstruction.
recently_processed.author: Imoto-Tar, T., Fung, M., Gurha, A.

recently_processed.title: Perceived social value is more strongly linked to gossip decisions with age in adolescence
recently_processed.content: Gossip is central to social exchange, yet how adolescents select what to share and with whom remains unclear. Across two independent samples aged 10-18 years (behavioural, n = 98; fMRI, n = 101 scanned), adolescents read information about absent third parties, chose whether and with whom to share it, and reported their appraisals. Sharing frequency showed no detectable age association. Valuation-to-decision coupling strengthened with age for interest in both samples, with a smaller age interaction for usefulness. Adolescents selected close friends more often with age when sharing. During scenario reading, before participants reported their choices, BOLD responses in a left inferior frontal cluster tracked subsequent interest ratings more strongly with age (n = 92), also within regions engaged by a separate mental-state judgment task. Together, these findings link age in adolescence to stronger valuation-to-decision coupling for interest and a greater proportion of sharing directed to close friends.
